title: Compass and Trail
premise: Tamsin Nakamura, a salvage diver who has spent fifteen years erasing himself from official records, is hired quietly to recover equipment from a wreck the navy refuses to acknowledge. When a government survey team vanishes near the river's forbidden headwaters—leaving their gear intact and no tracks—he realizes the wreck, the vanishing, and his own buried past are threads of the same cover-up. Following the river upstream with a defector from the survey team, Tamsin uncovers a hidden installation where the state has been weaponizing the water source itself, and confronts the man who erased his identity years ago. In the end, Tamsin chooses exposure over invisibility: he floods the installation's records into the open, accepts arrest as the price of justice outside the law, and finally measures his life in truth rather than miles.
about_author: Odile Underhill is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent a decade mapping rivers she was never permitted to name. She writes adventure fiction from a houseboat on an unnamed tributary, where she keeps her charts locked in a lead-lined case.

chapters.title: Fathoms and Silence
chapters.summary: Tamsin dives a wrecked navy vessel off-limits to civilians, recovering a sealed case he was paid to ignore. His POV establishes his meticulous anonymity—no records, no fixed address, life measured in miles logged. The emotional beat is controlled unease: the case hums with technology fifteen years ahead of anything salvage should hold.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Tamsin traces his anonymous employer through dead-drop payments and finds the trail ends at a shell company tied to the government survey office. POV alternates briefly with Mara Voss, a survey cartographer, introducing the vanished team. The beat is paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Hired unofficially to investigate the vanished survey team, Tamsin reaches their last camp: tents pitched, instruments running, meals half-eaten, no bodies, no tracks—not even insect interference. His POV; the beat is dread, because he recognizes the signature of a cleanup he once helped bury.

chapters.title: Mara Voss, Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: Mara, the team's sole survivor hiding in a ranger cabin, confronts Tamsin at knifepoint before trusting him. Her POV reveals the team found something upstream that rewrote their maps overnight. The beat is two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The River Forbids It
chapters.summary: They learn the headwaters sit inside a jurisdiction so classified it appears on no public map—a blank Tamsin has seen before on charts from his old life. His POV; flashback fragments surface for the first time in fifteen years. The beat is the past knocking.

chapters.title: Downstream Informants
chapters.summary: In a river town, a retired ferryman trades information for silence about his own crimes, revealing supply barges moving upstream at night under naval escort. Mara's POV; she begins redrawing the blank map from rumor. The beat is fragile alliance.

chapters.title: What the Water Carries
chapters.summary: Testing the river downstream, they find trace compounds that shouldn't exist naturally—something at the source is changing the water itself. Tamsin's POV connects the wreck's cargo to the compound. The beat is revelation with teeth.

chapters.title: The Man Who Erased Him
chapters.summary: A flash drive in the survey gear contains personnel files—including Tamsin Nakamura's original name and the operation that wiped it. His POV, raw and unguarded for the first time. The beat is grief disguised as anger.

chapters.title: Patrol Lines
chapters.summary: Naval patrols tighten the river; the pair must run a checkpoint at night using salvage-diving tricks to pass beneath hull sensors. Alternating POV during the escape. The beat is kinetic fear and deepening trust.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: The old ferryman offers his last barge as far as the gorge, asking only that they make the record true before he dies. Mara's POV; she confesses she signed the classification order that blinded her own team. The beat is complicity examined.

chapters.title: Gorge of the Unmapped
chapters.summary: The barge is scuttled by a patrol boat; Tamsin and Mara dive the gorge rapids to survive, losing most of their evidence. His POV underwater, where he is most himself. The beat is loss that clarifies resolve.

chapters.title: Source Country
chapters.summary: Above the gorge they cross into terrain absent from every map, finding survey markers dated decades back—the cover-up predates everyone hunting them. Mara's POV recalibrates the scale of the conspiracy. The beat is awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Installation
chapters.summary: They reach the headwaters: a facility built into the spring itself, extracting and refining the compound for use as an untraceable control agent in municipal water systems. Tamsin's POV; he sees his own past work echoed in its design. The beat is recognition and revulsion.

chapters.title: Director Hale
chapters.summary: Captured, Tamsin faces Director Hale—the man who erased him—who offers restoration of his identity in exchange for silence. Their duel of words forms the chapter's spine. The beat is temptation offered precisely where the wound is deepest.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Imprisoned in the facility, Tamsin weighs Hale's offer while Mara, still free, infiltrates the records vault. His POV in solitary dark; the beat is the temptation of becoming someone again versus remaining no one with a conscience.

chapters.title: Vault of Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Mara reaches the archive and discovers decades of disappeared people—all given Tamsin's treatment—catalogued by Hale personally. Her POV; the beat is fury transmuted into method: she copies everything, twice.

chapters.title: Upstream Flood
chapters.summary: Mara triggers the facility's emergency discharge, flooding lower levels and freeing Tamsin amid chaos. Escape sequence with alternating POV. The beat is momentum—fifteen years of running finally pointed in one direction.

chapters.title: Hale at the Spring
chapters.summary: At the source itself, Tamsin confronts Hale physically and morally; Hale argues that controlled water is controlled peace. Tamsin chooses to destroy the extraction core rather than take the deal. The beat is the climax: identity claimed by action, not paperwork.

chapters.title: The River Decides
chapters.summary: The collapsing facility releases the compound harmlessly diluted as the river reclaims its course; they ride the flood down the gorge on wreckage. Tamsin's POV, alive in a way he hasn't been since before the erasure. The beat is catharsis.

chapters.title: Records in Open Water
chapters.summary: Downstream, they broadcast the archive to every newsroom and foreign desk they can reach, knowing capture is certain. Mara's POV, steady at last. The beat is sacrifice made deliberate rather than accidental.

chapters.title: Arrest at Mile Zero
chapters.summary: Authorities take Tamsin at the river's mouth as the story breaks worldwide; Hale's network fractures under exposure. His POV, hands cuffed, watching the water carry the truth seaward. The beat is justice achieved outside the law, at the law's doorstep.

chapters.title: Measured in Truth
chapters.summary: Months later, testifying under his restored birth name, Tamsin declines witness protection and returns to diving—but now charts rivers openly, teaching Mara's students. Final image: a map with nothing blank on it. The beat is resolution: a life measured not in miles fled but in truths told.
